rendered_prompt:
Write a short paragraph explaining to a new volunteer how the tool library lends out power drills and what happens if one comes back damaged.

Requirements -- your response must satisfy every one of these:
Do not use the letter e anywhere in your response, including inside words.
Do not use bulleted or numbered lists.
target_output: At our tool library, show your ID, sign our loan log, and pick a drill for a short loan. Staff will show its main parts and how to run it with caution, and you must bring it back by its loan day. If a drill is hurt or will not run, notify us promptly; staff will look at it, and you may pay for a fix or a full swap if harm was from poor handling.

Write a paragraph for a museum label describing a restored printing press and what visitors can watch it do on demonstration days.

Requirements -- your response must satisfy every one of these:
Do not use any of these words: coffee, espresso, latte, lattes.
Do not use any of these phrases: in conclusion, to sum up.
Do not use the letter e anywhere in your response, including inside words.
target_output: This historic iron printmaking apparatus, brought back to full working form, shows how ink and muscular skill put words onto stock prior to digital tools. On program days, visitors may watch staff ink small alloy sorts, lock sorts into a form, lay a stock slip atop it, and pull its long arm. A pull puts dark, crisp words onto a blank slip, bringing old shop craft back into action.
